text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The government does not expect to increase public pensions in 1998.

- Peter Wittmann, state secretary in the Finance Ministry, wants to think about a Danish proposal to restructure the European Union's regional subsidy fund. European subsidies to companies in Austria have reached about 26 percent of the maximum level of 21.8 billion schillings.
- Two top Viennese managers in Hong Kong see good economic chances for Vienna as a loaction.

- Far-right Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider says Austria should join NATO for economic reasons. Conservative party whip Andreas Khol says the discovery of Soviet arms depots in Austria confirm his belief that neutrality is ineffective.
- Canadian car parts supplier Magna will set up a metal pressing plant in Styria. The company will invest 700 million schillings and create 200 new jobs.
- Die Erste savings bank will take over GiroCredit's Sparinvest after buying Bank Austria's stake in GiroCredit.

- Chancellor Viktor Klima confirms the government does not plan to introduce new austerity measures in its 1998 and 1999 budgets. However, he said he would put pressure on ministries to save money and increase efficiency.
- Both Austria's constitutional court and the European Comission will look into Austria Tabak's sales monopoly.
- Import of private weapons is increasing. Gun control laws are soft in eastern Europe while the debate about stricter hand gun control laws in Austria is growing.
- John Kornblum, an advisor to the U.S., says Austria is welcome to join NATO anytime.
- Chancellor Klima says his party does not want to slow down talks about Austria joining NATO.
- New U.N. general secretary Kofi Annan, on his first visit to Vienna, has confirmed the city's importance as a U.N. location. However he expects major spending cuts.
- Brickmaker Wienerberger's chief Erhard Schaschl has denied reports his company plans to sell its unit Treibacher.

- Regional energy provider Bewag's chief executive Werner Kasztler says cheaper industrial electricity prices should not be paid for by private households. He calls for closer cooperation within the industry.
- Russian arms producer Mapo wants to sell its MiG air fighters to the Austrian army which is expected to renew its fleet in the near future.
